title: Talking about beliefs and opinions
about: Collocations for saying what you believe and think: firmly believe, share sb's opinion, a sneaking suspicion, cast doubt on, opinions are divided. The last part covers common mistakes such as wish instead of hope and heavy instead of strong opinions.

parts.title: More formal ways of discussing beliefs

items.pattern: firmly / strongly believe (that) … · firmly believe in sth / in doing sth
items.meaning: believe something very strongly and feel sure you are right
items.example: I **firmly believe** that children should learn to swim before they're seven.
more: My grandmother **firmly believes** that a cold shower in the morning keeps you healthy.
We **firmly believe** in eating together as a family at least once a day.
items.watchOut: «Твердо вірю» — firmly believe або strongly believe, не hard believe і не solidly believe. Firmly зазвичай стоїть перед believe: I firmly believe that…

items.pattern: share sb's opinion / view (on / about sth) · share the opinion / view that …
items.meaning: have the same opinion as someone else
items.example: I **share your opinion** on the new bus timetable: it's much worse than the old one.
more: Not everyone in my family **shares my view** about getting up early at weekends.
My neighbours **share the opinion** that the street needs more trees.
items.watchOut: «Поділяю вашу думку» — I share your opinion (view). Не divide і не split: вони означають «ділити на частини». Далі — on або about: share sb's opinion on sth.

items.phrase: be a great believer in sth
items.pattern: be a great / firm / big believer in sth / in doing sth
items.meaning: think that something is good, useful or important
items.uk: бути великим прихильником чогось, свято вірити в користь чогось
items.example: My dad's **a great believer in** fresh air: he opens the windows even in January.
more: I'm **a great believer in** writing shopping lists. It saves money.
The hotel owner is **a great believer in** home-made food.
items.watchOut: Після believer — in: a great believer in sth, не of і не to. Замість great кажуть firm або, розмовно, big. Не плутай із fan, де інший прийменник: a big fan of sth.

items.pattern: contrary to popular belief, … · contrary to popular opinion
items.meaning: although many people think so, it is not true
items.example: **Contrary to popular belief**, goldfish can remember things for months.
more: **Contrary to popular belief**, you don't need expensive shoes to start running.
**Contrary to popular belief**, our little town isn't boring: there's lots to do at weekends.
items.watchOut: «Всупереч» — contrary to, не opposite to і не against. «Поширена думка» — popular belief: popular тут означає «поширений серед людей». Наголос: contrary /ˈkɒntrəri/ — на перший склад.

items.pattern: have (good / every) reason to believe (that) … · there is reason to believe
items.meaning: have facts or information that make you think something is true
items.example: We **have reason to believe** that the cat is hiding in the neighbours' shed.
more: Is there any **reason to believe** the train will be late?
The doctor **has every reason to believe** you'll be fine in a week.
items.watchOut: «Маю підстави вважати» — have reason to believe: reason тут зазвичай без артикля. Підсилити можна словами good або every: We have every reason to believe… Те саме значення — have grounds to believe.

items.pattern: A and B are poles apart (in / on sth) · be poles apart when it comes to sth
items.meaning: be completely different, for example in opinions, tastes or character
items.uk: бути цілковитими протилежностями, різнитися як небо і земля
items.example: My sister and I are **poles apart** when it comes to holidays: she loves beaches, I love mountains.
more: The two candidates are **poles apart** on the question of parking in the town centre.
My parents are **poles apart** in character, but they've been happily married for forty years.
items.watchOut: «Різні як небо і земля» — poles apart (або worlds apart). Завжди множина poles і без артикля: we're poles apart, не the poles apart.

items.pattern: it's a matter of opinion (whether …) · that's a matter of opinion
items.meaning: people have different opinions about this and nobody can say who is right
items.uk: це питання смаку, тут кожен має свою думку
items.example: Whether the new kitchen looks better than the old one is **a matter of opinion**.
more: "This is the best pizza in town." "Well, that's **a matter of opinion**."
It's **a matter of opinion** whether dogs or cats make better pets.
items.watchOut: Не a question of meaning: meaning — «значення», а не «думка». That's a matter of opinion часто звучить як м'яка незгода: «Ну, це ще як подивитися».

items.pattern: have a difference of opinion (with sb / about sth) · there's a difference of opinion
items.meaning: a disagreement; often a polite way of saying an argument
items.example: I had a small **difference of opinion** with the waiter about the bill.
more: My sister and I had **a difference of opinion** about where to put the Christmas tree.
There's **a difference of opinion** at work about whether the windows should be open or closed.
items.watchOut: Зазвичай opinion тут в однині: a difference of opinion. Це м'який, ввічливий спосіб сказати, що люди не погодилися чи навіть посварилися. Дієслово — have: I had a difference of opinion with…

items.pattern: have (got) a sneaking suspicion (that) …
items.meaning: begin to think something is true, although you aren't sure
items.uk: у мене закрадається підозра, мене бере підозра
items.example: I've **got a sneaking suspicion** that we've taken the wrong turning.
more: She had **a sneaking suspicion** that her son hadn't done his homework.
I have **a sneaking suspicion** I left the iron on.
items.watchOut: Sneaking — «що підкрадається»: підозра з'являється тихо й поступово, часто про те, у що не хочеться вірити. Дієслово — have або have got. Розмовно кажуть і a sneaky suspicion.

items.pattern: make assumptions (about sb / sth) · make the assumption that …
items.meaning: think something is true without enough evidence
items.example: Don't **make assumptions** about people because of the clothes they wear.
more: We **made the assumption** that everyone at the party spoke English.
Teachers shouldn't **make assumptions** about which children will do well.
items.watchOut: «Робити припущення» — make assumptions, не do assumptions. Assumption часто означає поспішний висновок без доказів. Нейтральна «здогадка» — a guess: make a guess.

items.pattern: an unshakeable belief / faith in sth · an unshakeable belief that …
items.meaning: a belief so strong that nothing can change it
items.example: My grandmother had **an unshakeable belief** in the power of chicken soup.
more: He has **an unshakeable belief** that his team will win the cup one day.
Her **unshakeable belief** in her son helped him through a difficult year.
items.watchOut: Британське написання — unshakeable, але правильне й unshakable. Belief — іменник, believe — дієслово: an unshakeable belief, не an unshakeable believe.

items.pattern: a set of beliefs / values / rules · sb's own set of beliefs
items.meaning: all the ideas a person believes in, seen together as one system
items.example: Every family has its own **set of beliefs** about how to bring up children.
more: Teenagers often start to question their parents' **set of beliefs**.
My grandparents and I have a very different **set of values**.
items.watchOut: «Система переконань» — a set of beliefs (або a belief system), не a group of beliefs: group — про людей або речі, зібрані разом. Так само a set of values, a set of rules.

items.pattern: sth colours sb's judgement / view / opinion
items.meaning: influence how someone thinks, so they can't judge fairly
items.uk: впливати на чиєсь судження, заважати судити неупереджено
items.example: Don't let one bad experience **colour your judgement** of the whole town.
more: Her love for her grandson **coloured her judgement**: she thought he could do no wrong.
Being hungry can **colour your judgement** when you're choosing food in a supermarket.
items.watchOut: Colour тут — дієслово: «забарвлювати», тобто впливати на судження, зазвичай однобоко. Схоже — cloud sb's judgement (затьмарювати). Британське написання — colour, judgement; американське — color, judgment.

items.pattern: sth leads sb to conclude / believe (that) … · lead – led – led
items.meaning: make someone decide that something is true after looking at the facts
items.uk: наводити когось на висновок, підводити до висновку
items.example: The muddy footprints **led me to conclude** that the dog had been in the garden.
more: Everything she said **led us to conclude** that she wasn't happy at her new school.
What **led you to conclude** that the hotel was too expensive?
items.watchOut: Lead – led – led. Після lead sb — to + дієслово: led us to conclude, а не led us conclude. «Зробити висновок» — reach / come to / draw a conclusion; make a conclusion звучить неприродно.

items.pattern: evidence / an opinion / a story is based on sth · base sth on sth
items.meaning: the evidence comes from that thing and depends on it
items.example: Your **evidence is based on** one conversation in a café. That's not enough.
more: The judge said the **evidence was based on** rumours, not facts.
The film **is based on** a true story.
items.watchOut: «Базується на» — is based on (пасив), а не is basing on і не bases on. Evidence — незлічуване: the evidence is, а не evidences are; один доказ — a piece of evidence.

items.pattern: attach (great / little / too much) importance to sth
items.meaning: think that something is important
items.example: My parents **attach great importance to** good manners at the table.
more: I don't **attach** much **importance to** horoscopes.
Some people **attach too much importance to** what car you drive.
items.watchOut: «Надавати значення» — attach importance to sth, прийменник — to. Не give importance і не pay importance: pay вживають з attention (pay attention to).

items.pattern: trust sb's judgement · (not) trust his / her judgement
items.meaning: believe that someone can make good decisions
items.example: I always **trust my sister's judgement** when I'm buying clothes.
more: Pick any restaurant you like. I **trust your judgement**.
After the last holiday he booked, I don't **trust his judgement** any more.
items.watchOut: «Довіряти судженню» — trust sb's judgement, зазвичай без in. Не believe her judgement: believe — вірити словам (I believe you), а trust — покладатися на людину, її рішення й вибір.

items.pattern: cast (serious) doubt on sth · cast – cast – cast
items.meaning: make people think that something may not be true or right
items.uk: ставити під сумнів, викликати сумніви щодо чогось
items.example: The new photos **cast doubt on** his story about being at home all evening.
more: A torn receipt **cast doubt on** the shop's claim that I had never paid.
Recent research has **cast doubt on** the idea that we need eight glasses of water a day.
items.watchOut: «Ставити під сумнів» — cast doubt on sth (або throw doubt on sth, call sth into question). Cast не змінюється: cast – cast – cast, не casted. Doubt вимовляється /daʊt/: b німа.

items.pattern: opinions are divided / opinion is divided (on / about / over sth)
items.meaning: people have different opinions about something
items.example: **Opinions are divided** on whether the town needs a new shopping centre.
more: In our house, **opinions are divided** about pineapple on pizza.
**Opinion is divided** over the new school uniform.
items.watchOut: «Думки розділилися» — opinions are divided (або split), не separated. Можна і в однині: opinion is divided. Далі — on, about або over.

items.pattern: my / sb's considered opinion is that … · in my considered opinion
items.meaning: an opinion you have after thinking about something carefully
items.example: My **considered opinion** is that we should wait until spring to paint the house.
more: After reading all the reviews, my **considered opinion** is that the cheaper phone is better.
Ask Grandad for his **considered opinion** before you sign anything.
items.watchOut: «Зважена думка» — considered opinion, не thoughtful opinion. І не considerate: considerate — «уважний, тактовний до інших» (a considerate neighbour).

items.pattern: have serious / grave misgivings about sth / about doing sth
items.meaning: have serious doubts or worries about whether something is right or will work
items.example: I **have serious misgivings about** letting a fourteen-year-old go to a festival alone.
more: Many parents **had serious misgivings about** the new school timetable.
She signed the contract, but she **had serious misgivings about** it.
items.watchOut: Misgivings — майже завжди множина, прийменник — about. Це сильніше, ніж просто doubts: є відчуття, що щось піде не так. Не heavy misgivings — кажуть serious або grave.

items.pattern: have (some / serious) doubts about sth · have my doubts
items.meaning: not be sure that something is true, good or will happen
items.uk: мати сумніви щодо чогось, сумніватися в чомусь
items.example: I **have doubts about** the accuracy of this weather app.
more: Mum **has doubts about** my plan to cycle to Scotland.
"Will he really pay us back?" "I **have my doubts**."
items.watchOut: «Сумніви в чомусь» — doubts about sth, не doubts in. Коротка ввічлива незгода: I have my doubts — «Я в цьому сумніваюся». Doubt вимовляється /daʊt/.

items.pattern: hope (that) sb will do sth · I hope you'll come / you can come
items.meaning: want something to happen and think it is possible
items.example: **I hope you'll come** to our housewarming on Saturday.
more: We **hope** the rain **will** stop before the match.
**I hope you can come**. It won't be the same without you.
items.watchOut: «Сподіваюся, що…» — I hope, не I wish. I wish you could come означає «шкода, що ти не можеш прийти». Після hope можна will або теперішній час: I hope you come / you'll come.

items.pattern: give up hope (of sth / of doing sth) · give up all hope
items.meaning: stop believing that something good will happen
items.example: We'd almost **given up hope** of finding a flat when the agent finally called.
more: Don't **give up hope**. Your bike might still turn up.
By the end of the season, the fans had **given up** all **hope** of winning the league.
items.watchOut: Без артикля: give up hope, а не give up the hope. Далі — of + -ing: give up hope of finding, а не to find. Синонім — lose hope.

items.pattern: think hard (about sth) · consider sth carefully
items.meaning: think very carefully and seriously about something
items.example: **Think hard** before you lend money to a friend.
more: I **thought hard** about the job offer all weekend.
We need to **consider** the cost **carefully** before we book.
items.watchOut: «Добре подумати» — think hard, не consider hard: з consider кажуть carefully (consider sth carefully). Не плутай hard (старанно, сильно) з hardly (ледве, майже не): I hardly thought about it — я майже не думав про це.

items.pattern: leave sb / sth alone
items.meaning: stop annoying someone, or stop touching something
items.uk: дати комусь спокій, залишити в спокої
items.example: I've got a headache. Please just **leave me alone** for an hour.
more: **Leave** the cat **alone**! She doesn't want to play.
**Leave** those biscuits **alone**. They're for the guests.
items.watchOut: «Дай мені спокій» — leave me alone; let me alone — застарілий варіант, сьогодні кажуть leave me alone. Let alone — інший вираз: «не кажучи вже про». І alone, а не lonely: lonely — «самотній, якому сумно».

items.pattern: hold the view / opinion that … · hold strong views on sth
items.meaning: have a particular opinion (a little formal)
items.example: Many doctors **hold the view** that children need more sleep than they get.
more: My uncle **holds the opinion** that summers were hotter when he was young.
Some parents **hold the view** that homework is a waste of time.
items.watchOut: «Дотримуватися думки» — hold the view / opinion, не keep the opinion. Meaning — «значення» (слова, фільму), а не «думка», тож hold the meaning тут не підходить. Можна також take the view that…

items.pattern: have strong opinions / views (on / about sth)
items.meaning: have very definite opinions and like to express them
items.example: My aunt **has strong opinions on** how to cook rice.
more: Both my grandmothers **have strong opinions** about how babies should sleep.
He **has strong views on** dogs in restaurants.
items.watchOut: «Тверді, категоричні погляди» — strong opinions / views, не heavy і не big opinions. Strong — головний партнер для opinion, view, belief, feeling.

warmup.uk: Я твердо вірю, що людям треба більше ходити пішки.
warmup.q: I ___ believe that people should walk more.
warmup.explain: Твердо вірити — firmly (або strongly) believe. Hard believe і tightly believe — кальки.

warmup.uk: Я поділяю твою думку щодо цього фільму.
warmup.q: I ___ your opinion of this film.
warmup.explain: Поділяти думку — share sb's opinion. Divide і split — ділити на частини.

warmup.uk: У нього дуже тверді погляди на виховання дітей.
warmup.q: He has very ___ opinions on bringing up children.
warmup.explain: Тверді, категоричні погляди — strong opinions. Heavy і big з opinions не вживають.

warmup.uk: Всупереч поширеній думці, верблюди не зберігають воду в горбах.
warmup.q: ___ to popular belief, camels don't store water in their humps.
warmup.explain: Всупереч поширеній думці — contrary to popular belief. Opposite to і against to тут не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Щодо грошей ми з братом цілковиті протилежності.
warmup.q: When it comes to money, my brother and I are ___ apart.
warmup.explain: Poles apart — як два полюси, кардинально різні. Так само кажуть worlds apart.

warmup.q: Opinions on the new park are ___.
warmup.explain: Думки розділилися — opinions are divided (або split).

warmup.uk: Сподіваюся, ти прийдеш на моє весілля.
warmup.q: I ___ you'll come to my wedding.
warmup.explain: Сподіватися — hope. Wish тут — помилка: I wish you could come означає «шкода, що ти не можеш прийти».
Дай мені спокій — leave me alone. Let alone — інший вираз: «не кажучи вже про».

A.q: My flatmate is super tidy and I'm really messy. We're ___ apart.
I ___ your opinion that the beach is too crowded in August.
A.explain: Поділяти чиюсь думку — share sb's opinion.

A.q: I've got a ___ suspicion that someone has eaten my yoghurt.
A.explain: У мене закрадається підозра — I've got a sneaking suspicion.

B.q: Opinions are ___ on the new parking rules: some people love them, some hate them.
Please don't ___ assumptions about what I can afford.
Several bad reviews have ___ doubt on the hotel's claim to be the best in town.
B.explain: Ставити під сумнів — cast doubt on sth (cast – cast – cast).

C.explain: Сподіваюся — I hope. Після wish не вживають will у такому значенні.

C.q: The paint is still wet, so leave the door ___.
C.explain: Leave sth alone — не чіпати. Lonely — самотній, сумний.

C.q: He has very ___ opinions about modern art.
C.explain: Тверді погляди — strong opinions, не heavy і не big.

example.title: The great dog debate
example.uk:
Думки в нашій родині щодо того, чи заводити собаку, розділилися. Мій син твердо переконаний, що кожній дитині потрібен домашній улюбленець, і я поділяю його думку. У таких питаннях ми з чоловіком зазвичай цілковиті протилежності, і в нього серйозні сумніви щодо цієї ідеї. Він каже, що квартира — не місце для собаки, але тут кожен має свою думку.

Учора за вечерею ми розійшлися в поглядах. Він сказав, що собакам потрібні години прогулянок, але, всупереч поширеній думці, деякі породи досить ліниві.

Я попросила його добре подумати, перш ніж казати «ні». Сьогодні вранці я побачила, як він розглядає цуценят в інтернеті. У мене закрадається підозра, що він передумує.
example.en:
[[Opinions are divided|b10]] in our family about getting a dog. My son [[firmly believes|a1]] that every child needs a pet, and I [[share his opinion|a2]]. My husband and I are usually [[poles apart|a6]] on things like this, and he [[has serious misgivings about|b12]] the idea. He says a flat is no place for a dog, but that's [[a matter of opinion|a7]].

Last night we had a [[difference of opinion|a8]] at dinner. He said dogs need hours of exercise, but [[contrary to popular belief|a4]], some breeds are quite lazy.

I asked him to [[think hard|c3]] before saying no. This morning I saw him looking at puppies online. I [[have a sneaking suspicion|a9]] he's changing his mind.
